_comment: Customer-facing narration, v2. Numbers here must match what the seeded gateway actually renders — 66 requests, $1.26, 1.4s average latency, 9 models with traffic, 51 configured models across 55 mappings, 5 unpriced mappings, and 46 production-price-ready models. Checked against the live API before recording, not written from memory.
_engine_note: <emphasis> is unsupported on the neural engine (InvalidSsmlException); phrasing comes from <break> and sentence shape instead.

scenes.ssml: <speak>Most teams reach a point where language models are running in five places, on three vendors, with no shared record of what any of it costs. <break time="500ms"/>AxonLLM is a control plane for that problem.</speak>
scenes.text: Most teams reach a point where language models are running in five places, on three vendors, with no shared record of what any of it costs. AxonLLM is a control plane for that problem.

scenes.ssml: <speak>It configures fifty-one models across thirteen provider adapters. Forty-six are production-price-ready with shipped pricing, all behind a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint. <break time="400ms"/>One wire format, whatever is answering underneath.</speak>
scenes.text: It configures 51 models across 13 provider adapters. Forty-six are production-price-ready with shipped pricing, all behind a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint. One wire format, whatever is answering underneath.

scenes.ssml: <speak>Every request crosses the same fifteen stages. <break time="400ms"/>Authentication, injection scanning, P-I-I redaction, then the quota hierarchy — organisation, business unit, project, environment. <break time="400ms"/>The budget check happens before a provider is billed, not after.</speak>
scenes.text: Every request crosses the same fifteen stages: authentication, injection scanning, PII redaction, then the quota hierarchy of organisation, business unit, project and environment. The budget check happens before a provider is billed, not after.

scenes.ssml: <speak>Adopting it is a one-line change. <break time="400ms"/>You keep the OpenAI SDK your code already uses and point its base U-R-L at the gateway. <break time="350ms"/>No new client library, no rewrite.</speak>
scenes.text: Adopting it is a one-line change. You keep the OpenAI SDK your code already uses and point its base URL at the gateway. No new client library, no rewrite.

scenes.ssml: <speak>Behind that one endpoint sit thirteen adapters — Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and the rest — each translated to a common format, including tool calls and streaming.</speak>
scenes.text: Behind that one endpoint sit thirteen adapters — Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and the rest — each translated to a common format, including tool calls and streaming.

scenes.ssml: <speak>This is the operator's view of a running gateway. <break time="450ms"/>Sixty-six requests, a dollar twenty-six of spend, and an eighty-seven point five percent cache hit rate across two projects. <break time="400ms"/>Ten providers, health-checked continuously — so cost and availability are things you watch, not things you reconstruct from an invoice.</speak>
scenes.text: This is the operator's view of a running gateway: 66 requests, $1.26 of spend, and an 87.5% cache hit rate across two projects. Ten providers, health-checked continuously, so cost and availability are things you watch, not things you reconstruct from an invoice.
scenes._verified: All four read off the live API at capture time. cache_hit_rate comes from /admin/overview (routes.py:179) and is cached / (cached + cache_creation) — of the tokens that touched the cache, the share that were reads. It is NOT cached/total_tokens, which is 3.9% and is a different question.

scenes.ssml: <speak>Every call is recorded individually. <break time="400ms"/>Which model answered, which provider served it, the user it belonged to, tokens, cost and latency — averaging about one-point-four seconds here. <break time="400ms"/>This is the audit trail, and it is one trail for all thirteen providers.</speak>
scenes.text: Every call is recorded individually: which model answered, which provider served it, the user it belonged to, tokens, cost and latency — averaging about 1.4 seconds here. This is the audit trail, and it is one trail for all thirteen providers.

scenes.ssml: <speak>The catalogue is where routing is configured. <break time="400ms"/>Each model carries its own strategy — least-latency, cost-optimised, or round-robin — and its own ordered list of providers to fall back through. <break time="400ms"/>Changing how traffic is routed does not touch application code.</speak>
scenes.text: The catalogue is where routing is configured. Each model carries its own strategy — least-latency, cost-optimised or round-robin — and its own ordered list of providers to fall back through. Changing how traffic is routed does not touch application code.

scenes.ssml: <speak>And this page is the one worth showing a sceptic. <break time="450ms"/>Five of fifty-five provider mappings have no verified price attached. Production excludes them from routing, leaving forty-six of fifty-one configured models production-price-ready with shipped pricing. <break time="400ms"/>The gateway makes the gap visible instead of serving an unpriced model.</speak>
scenes.text: And this page is the one worth showing a sceptic. Five of 55 provider mappings have no verified price attached. Production excludes them from routing, leaving 46 of 51 configured models production-price-ready with shipped pricing. The gateway makes the gap visible instead of serving an unpriced model.

scenes.ssml: <speak>One API, every model, full control. <break time="450ms"/>AxonLLM is open source under M-I-T zero, and runs with a single docker compose command.</speak>
scenes.text: One API, every model, full control. AxonLLM is open source under MIT-0, and runs with a single docker compose command.
